item.title: What the Twin Revolts Against Flock and Data Centers Tell Us About the Power and Risks of Populism
item.description:
America is in the grip of two targeted anti-tech backlashes. The first is against automatic license plate readers (ALPRs), which are mostly, but not exclusively, supplied to thousands of local police departments by the company Flock Safety. The second is against data centers writ large: large boxy facilities housing rows of servers doing everything from hosting streaming services to powering advances in AI. Neither technology is particularly new. Police departments have been using ALPRs for decades. Data centers predate the internet. That makes the sudden negative turn against both so startling. item.title: El Niño Has Become a Doom Loop
item.description:
In the middle of the Pacific Ocean, along the equator, scientists have drawn a box. It’s a big box, two-thirds the size of China, yet hardly anyone lives inside it. This rectangular swath of open ocean is monitored by satellites and a network of moored buoys that measure minute changes in the temperature of the water, with an eye toward anomalies. Every few years or so, driven by changing winds and currents, the water temperature in this part of the ocean starts to rise; even a half degree Celsius above normal over months warrants a designation that an El Niño phase has begun. That’s enough warming to unleash floods and fires, drought and famine, around the world. The box is called Niño 3.4.
